constants.doc: byte length of a v0 batch header (fact: enc.len)
byte length of a v1 batch header (adds lastBlockNumber)
byte length of a v2 batch header (reuses the v1 wire format; the 32-byte field at offset 57 becomes an aggregate hash)
constants.note: v2 has no dedicated codec library; the contract decodes v2 headers through the v1 codec (257 bytes) and interprets offset 57 differently

constants.doc: largest batch header version accepted on-chain
versioned hash of the all-zero blob: 0x01 || sha256(0xc0 || 0^47)[1:]
EIP-4844 blob payload capacity: 4096 field elements x 31 bytes
constants.reason: payload capacity is only meaningful off-chain; on-chain the contract sees blobhash commitments, not blob bytes

constants.doc: per-transaction blob ceiling used when re-sealing replayed batches
constants.reason: replay-time protocol cap; the contract bounds blobs per commit through calldata/blobhash presence, not this constant

constants.doc: the contract writes a constant zero into the sequencerSetVerifyHash field at offset 185 (fact: enc_sol zero-write; the M0 equality law was refuted because Go copies the producer's field)
constants.note: Solidity emits the constant bytes32(0); Go copies the header field. The agreement condition (producer writes zero) is an M0 refutation witness, recorded here as an asymmetric link rather than an equality.
